Shadow bundles are Medicare claims data for items and services and their associated payments constructed into discrete procedural- and/or condition-specific acute episodes of care.  FIPS_CHAR: 13-character FIPS code for a given block group. Can be broken into codes for state (digits 1-2), county (digits 3-5), tract (digits 6-11), and block group (digit 12), prefixed by "G".  Suppression flags: GQ: High group quarters population PH: Low population and/or housing

releases.name: medicare_monthly_enrollment_dashboard
releases.description: Re-implement the Medicare Monthly Enrollment dashboard in an open-source framework that could be deployed to data.cms.gov in the future.
releases.longDescription: An open source re-implementation of the CMS Medicare Monthly Enrollment dashboard, built as a static site with Eleventy and the U.S. Web Design System. The dashboard visualizes the Medicare Monthly Enrollment dataset published on data.cms.gov, which it queries directly from the browser through the public CMS Data API rather than through a bespoke backend. Users can explore national, state, and county level enrollment trends over time, compare Original Medicare against Medicare Advantage and Other Health Plan enrollment, drill from a national choropleth map into the counties of an individual state, and review the underlying figures in an accessible data grid. The project exists to show that the dashboard can be rebuilt with an open source stack and no proprietary dependencies, so that the code, the visualizations, and the accessibility work behind them can be reused by other teams and potentially deployed to data.cms.gov in the future.

releases.name: npd
releases.description: A modern version of a health provider directory to serve as a single source of truth for the benefit of all
releases.longDescription: The CMS National Provider Directory addresses fragmented healthcare provider data that costs the industry an estimated $2.76 billion annually. Currently, provider information is duplicated and corrected across over 5,000 systems, leading to widespread inaccuracy. NPD creates a unified FHIR-compliant directory combining data from CMS sources (NPPES, PECOS) and industry partners into a single authoritative source. Built with Django REST Framework and React, the system provides APIs and a search interface for accessing provider practices, addresses, specialties, licenses, quality scores, insurance plan participation, and interoperability endpoints. By serving as the definitive provider directory, NPD reduces data collection burden on providers and payers while improving accuracy for over 100 million Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries.

releases.name: npd_VEINHasher
releases.description: Generates a secure, hashed representation of an Employer Identification Number (EIN).
releases.longDescription: An Employer Identification Number (EIN) is a unique 9-digit federal tax identification number assigned by the IRS to businesses operating within the United States. This project provides a secure and standardized hashing mechanism for EINs so downstream systems can verify and reference EINs without directly storing sensitive identifiers. It is intended for use in operational pipelines where privacy and security controls require strong hashing for regulated data elements.

It supports interoperability analysis, HTI-2 compliance assessments, and downstream structured data transformation, enabling consistent and secure integrations across provider systems. The tooling automates discovery, retrieval, normalization, and export of FHIR server metadata to better support federal interoperability requirements.

releases.name: repo-sunsetter
releases.description: A GitHub Action that prepares a repository for archival by automating documentation updates and providing a review checklist
releases.longDescription: repo-sunsetter is a comprehensive GitHub action that prepares a repository for archival. It performs 3 steps to "sunset" a repository:  adds an archival notice to the README.md to inform users about the state of the repository, update project metadata by marking project as archived in code.json, and files an issue containing an archival checklist based on the repository's maturity model tier where the checklist contains various tasks reviewing the contents of the repository.

releases.name: repodive-tools
releases.description: Scripts and tools to gather information about git repositories.
releases.longDescription: This repository is a collection of scripts and tools for a given repodiving effort. Repodiving in this context means going through a git repository and gathering relevant information for a specific purpose.

releases.name: repolinter-actions
releases.description: Run Repolinter in your CI pipeline with the option to send PRs
releases.longDescription: This fork extends the original repolinter-action by allowing users to automatically create Pull Requests that fix compliance issues. When Repolinter detects missing files or required content, it creates a Pull Request with the necessary files and content based on templates defined in your repolinter configuration.

releases.name: share-it-act-lp
releases.description: Guide to the SHARE IT Act helping federal agencies comply with source code sharing requirements
releases.longDescription: The Source Code Harmonization And Reuse in Information Technology Act (SHARE IT Act) requires federal agencies to share custom-developed software code, including metadata about the project, with each other to eliminate duplicative government work. This website provides comprehensive documentation that goes more in depth into the SHARE IT Act and provides tooling and guidance to help users become compliant.

releases.longDescription: The CMS OSPO has created automated metadata generation processes and tooling for the agency's 10,000+ repositories that we estimate can reduce processing time from 1 hour (minimum) to ~10 minutes per repository.

releases.name: super-changelog
releases.description: SuperChangelog is a tool for aggregating CHANGELOG.md files from individual repositories into one SUPERCHANGELOG
releases.longDescription: Super-changelog is an automated system for tracking organization-wide changes across all public repositories in a GitHub organization. It uses Python scripts to gather metadata, track changes, generate structured updates, and publish them in multiple formats. The project currently creates pull requests with updated data, and includes optional, but fully configured integrations for email and Slack notifications. This repository contains the source code for all the supporting automation scripts.

releases.name: year-in-review
releases.description: A Year in Review prototype documenting the OSPOs impact and activity.
releases.longDescription: A single-page, self-contained web report that summarizes a year of the CMS Open Source Program Office activity and impact on GitHub. Inspired by the Twitter Open Source Year in Review format, the prototype reframes standard OSS health metrics — commits, contributors, stars, watchers, forks, and merged pull requests — around the DSACMS repository maturity model, in which a project growth is visualized as a tree maturing from a private seedling (Tier 0) to a community-governed tree (Tier 4).
